channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Ministro do STJ critica interferência em ações e diz que 'todo mundo está vendendo voto'
item.description: Minister João Otávio de Noronha of the Superior Tribunal of Justice (STJ) criticized external interference in ongoing court cases, stating that 'Brasília is very difficult' and that 'everyone is selling votes around, all over Brazil'. He emphasized the severity of the situation during a session of the Fourth Panel of the tribunal.

item.title: Lula pede mobilização a centrais sindicais para fim da escala 6x1
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva received 68 demands from union representatives after sending to Congress a bill to reduce the workweek to 40 hours (ending the 6x1 schedule), urging workers to mobilize for its approval. Lula emphasized the need for union pressure, criticized the 2017 Labor Reform and 2019 Pension Reform as setbacks, and honored activist Rick Azevedo, who inspired the bill after experiencing burnout. The event also warned against opposition proposals to increase work hours, similar to those in Argentina.

item.title: Projetos de renaturalização de rios avançam no Brasil para combater enchentes
item.description: River renaturalization projects are advancing in Brazil, with initiatives in São Paulo (Tietê, Pinheiros, Bixiga Creek), Rio de Janeiro (Limpa Rio Margens), and Piauí (Parnaíba basin), signaling a paradigm shift from rigid containment to ecological recovery and multifunctional use. These efforts combine drainage, sanitation, riverside redevelopment, and public access, highlighted by a R$9 billion PPP slated for auction in 2026 and the Integra Tietê program aiming to cut organic load by 54% by 2029.

item.title: Ramagem ganha liberdade nos EUA após 2 dias de detenção
item.description: Former federal deputy Alexandre Ramagem (PL-RJ) was released on Wednesday (15) after two days of detention by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in Florida. He had fled Brazil in September 2025 to avoid serving a 16-year sentence for his role in the 2022 coup plot, using a diplomatic passport irregularly. His release comes as Brazil's extradition request awaits a response from the U.S. government.

item.title: Lula critica o fim do imposto sindical
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized the abolition of the union tax, which was eliminated by the 2017 labor reform, claiming the previous government financially strangled unions while business owners retained privileges like the S System. He made the remarks during a meeting with union centrals to deliver the Workers' Class Agenda, which includes 68 demands for 2026–2030, such as reducing the workweek without cutting wages and ending the 6X1 schedule. The government also sent an urgent bill to Congress to abolish the 6X1 work schedule, coinciding with the Workers' Class March in Brasília.

item.title: 'Foram dias duros', diz mulher de Ramagem após soltura de ex-diretor da Abin nos EUA pelo ICE
item.description: The wife of Alexandre Ramagem, Rebeca Ramagem, released a video after her husband's release by ICE agents in the U.S., describing his detention as 'hard days, of pain and injustice' and alleging persecution. She reiterated her support for pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, while allies credited the release to the Trump administration, though U.S. authorities did not confirm the detention stemmed from a minor traffic violation.

item.title: A troca de farpas entre Gilmar Mendes e Romeu Zema
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes rebutted criticisms from former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema, who had labeled the court 'corrupt' and called for the removal and arrest of justices. Mendes highlighted the contradiction in Zema's stance, noting that the former governor benefited from STF rulings that suspended Minas Gerais' debt payments to the Union—estimated at R$ 165 billion—but now attacks the Court when its decisions oppose his political interests.

item.title: Lula critica ‘pejotização’ e pede reunião de centrais sindicais com Gilmar Mendes
item.description: President Lula criticized pejotization in a meeting with union leaders, stating that the practice of hiring workers as legal entities harms employees, Social Security, FGTS, and public housing and sanitation policies. He urged unions to schedule a meeting with Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes, who is the rapporteur of a case assessing the constitutionality of pejotization, to expose its harms. Lula also attacked the labor and pension reforms of Temer and Bolsonaro, claiming they 'buried' workers' rights.

item.title: Ramagem é solto nos EUA 2 dias após ser preso pelo ICE
item.description: Alexandre Ramagem, former head of Brazil's intelligence agency Abin and sentenced to 16 years in prison by the STF for coup attempt, was detained by ICE in the U.S. on April 13, 2026, and released two days later, according to Paulo Figueiredo and Eduardo Bolsonaro. He had been a fugitive since his conviction, with the crimes committed while holding public office.

item.title: Governo Lula piora trajetória de projeção da dívida até 2035
item.description: Brazil's general government gross debt (DBGG) is now projected to reach 87.8% of GDP in 2029, up from the previous forecast of 84.2% peaking in 2028, according to the Ministry of Finance. The debt-to-GDP ratio rose from 71.7% at the end of 2022 to 79.2% in February 2025, driven by high interest rates (Selic), persistent primary deficits, and rising public spending. The exclusion of R$ 347 billion in precatory payments from the primary surplus target until 2035, as proposed in the new LDO, was cited as a key factor worsening the debt trajectory between 2025 and 2026.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes representa contra Alessandro Vieira na PGR por abuso em relatório da CPI
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes has submitted a representation to the Attorney General’s Office (PGR) against Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) for alleged abuse of authority in the Organized Crime CPI, after Vieira drafted a report calling for the indictment of STF ministers and the PGR. The report was rejected by a 6-4 vote in the CPI, with Mendes arguing Vieira acted with improper purpose, attempting to criminalize justices without concrete evidence and using the investigation for electoral purposes.

item.title: Lula critica fim do imposto sindical e diz que movimento foi asfixiado
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized the end of the mandatory union tax, stating it was an attempt to asphyxiate the union movement, similar to how the government aims to combat organized crime by cutting off its financial resources. He noted that while unions lost funding, business elites retain advantages like the S System, and questioned the current state of union centrals. Lula received the 'Workers' Class Agenda' and a red cap reading 'For the end of the 6×1 schedule', highlighting labor demands for the 2026–2030 period.

item.title: Motta diz que votação da PEC da escala 6x1 será dia 22 na CCJ
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta confirmed that the PEC ending the 6x1 work scale will be voted in the Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) on April 22, after the Tiradentes holiday, due to requests for extended review by deputies. He stated he will prioritize the PEC over the government’s bill to reduce the weekly workweek to 40 hours, despite denying any tension with President Lula. The issue is becoming a political prominence dispute, as the PEC is a key flag in Lula’s re-election campaign.

item.title: Lula manda projeto de LDO com meta de superavit de R$ 73,2 bi em 2027
item.description: The Lula government will send to Congress an LDO bill setting a primary surplus target of R$ 73.2 billion (0.5% of GDP) for 2027, with gradual increases to 1.5% of GDP by 2030. Despite the official target, the economic team estimates that in 2026 the primary surplus will be only R$ 3.5 billion, near the floor of 0% of GDP. The gradual inclusion of precatory payments starting in 2027 — with 10% of the stock added annually to fiscal targets — poses a challenge to public accounts, although the 2025 Precatory PEC has so far avoided discretionary spending cuts.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro agradece a Trump pela soltura de Ramagem nos EUA
item.description: Former deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro thanked U.S. President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio for the release of Alexandre Ramagem, former PF director and cassed federal deputy, who was detained at an ICE facility in Orlando after losing his diplomatic passport. Ramagem, sentenced by the STF to 16 years in prison for his role in the coup plot, had been held since April 13 over immigration issues and is now free in the U.S., where he has lived with his family since September 2025.

item.title: Flávio acusa Moraes de usar STF para interferir nas eleições
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president in 2026, accused Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes of attempting to interfere in elections through judicial rulings, now that he is no longer on the TSE. He stated that such practices cannot be accepted in 2026 and that there is a clear strategy to disrupt the election.

item.title: Alexandre Ramagem deixa a prisão nos Estados Unidos
item.description: Alexandre Ramagem leaves U.S. immigration detention after being held for migration issues. He was sentenced by the STF to 16 years in prison for attempting a coup, fled Brazil clandestinely in 2025 via Roraima-Guyana-U.S., and the PF awaits details on his release. While abroad, he faced administrative and political sanctions: his federal deputy mandate was revoked, his diplomatic passport cancelled, and his parliamentary wages blocked by the STF.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro diz que Alexandre Ramagem foi solto nos Estados Unidos
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro claimed that Alexandre Ramagem, former head of Brazil's intelligence agency Abin and a fugitive from Brazilian justice, was released by U.S. prison authorities after being detained by ICE. He credited the release to President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, stating Ramagem is now home with his family and deserves asylum in the 'land of freedom.' The Federal Police had said the arrest resulted from Brazil-U.S. cooperation, but Ramagem’s allies denied this, saying he would be freed once his asylum status was clarified.

item.title: Após decisão de Mendonça, STJ retira provas de ação contra ex-governador do Acre
item.description: The STJ removed evidence from the criminal action against former Acre governor Gladson Cameli, complying with a decision by Supreme Court Minister André Mendonça that nullified financial intelligence reports from Coaf between 2020 and 2021. Reporter Nancy Andrighi stated the removal does not affect the trial, as the evidence was not used in the indictment or her vote, and the case stands on other proof. Cameli, who resigned to run for Senate in 2026, was voted by Andrighi for conviction to 25 years and 9 months in prison, a fine, and R$ 11 million in damages for public fund diversion and fraud.

item.title: Lula liga para Motta após eleição de petista ao TCU
item.description: President Lula called House Speaker Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB) after the election of PT deputy Odair Cunha (PT-MG) to the Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) with 303 votes, to thank him for his support. The vote surprised deputies, as Lula had doubted the approval given the competition. Motta’s support for Odair was part of a political deal: the PT backed his 2025 speakership bid in exchange for his TCU vote.

item.title: Lula chama Bolsonaro de “a coisa que veio depois do Temer”
item.description: Lula called Bolsonaro 'the thing that came after Temer' during a meeting with trade union centrals, criticizing both for their labor reforms that, he said, precarized work and pensions. He defended the Workers' Class Agenda, which includes reducing the workweek to 40 hours without pay cuts and ending the 6x1 schedule, already sent to Congress under urgency.

item.title: Gilmar aciona a PGR contra Alessandro Vieira por relatório da CPI do Crime Organizado
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes has asked the Attorney General's Office to investigate Senator Alessandro Vieira for alleged abuse of authority and arbitrariness in drafting the report of the Organized Crime CPI, in which Vieira proposed indicting Mendes and other STF ministers for crimes of responsibility. The report was rejected by the committee 6-4, and Gilmar argued the proposal lacks factual basis, exceeds the CPI's scope, and conflates penal with administrative matters.

item.title: EXPO Turismo Paulista consolida estâncias como vitrine
item.description: The 1st Paulista Tourism Expo, organized by APRECESP, brought together 69 tourist resorts from São Paulo State at the Anhembi District, showcasing destinations, culture, gastronomy, and business opportunities. Held during a record year for Brazilian tourism — R$ 195.7 billion in 2025, with São Paulo contributing R$ 78.6 billion — the event emphasized the sector’s strategic importance for job creation, income, and regional development. Officials including Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, Culture Secretary Marília Marton, and SEBRAE/SP Director Nelson Hervey da Costa attended, highlighting public-private partnerships as key to strengthening municipal tourism.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes pede a Gonet que investigue Alessandro Vieira na PGR
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes has requested that Prosecutor General Paulo Gonet investigate Senator Alessandro Vieira for alleged abuse of authority in the Organized Crime CPI. Mendes argues Vieira acted illegally by proposing the indictment of STF ministers and Gonet himself without concrete evidence, confusing administrative infractions with criminal offenses and exceeding the commission’s investigative powers. The CPI rejected Vieira’s report by a 6-4 vote, which Mendes cites as proof of the initiative’s improper purpose.

item.title: Escala 6x1: Motta marca votação de proposta em comissão para 22 de abril
item.description: Chamber President Arthur Lira (PP-AL) announced that the vote on the report regarding the bill to end the 6x1 work scale in the CCJ will take place on April 22, following a delay due to opposition requests for view. He reiterated that the PEC’s timetable remains unchanged despite the executive’s urgent constitutional bill, asserting the Chamber president’s authority over the legislative agenda. Rapporteur Deputy Paulo Azi (União Brasil-BA) affirmed the bill’s constitutionality, proposed a transition phase and compensation for productive sectors, and stressed the need for consensus to avoid pitting workers against employers.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes pede que PGR investigue relator da CPI por possível abuso de autoridade após tentativa de indiciamento
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes has asked the Prosecutor General's Office to investigate Senator Alessandro Vieira for alleged abuse of authority, after Vieira proposed indicting STF ministers in the final report of the Organized Crime CPI, which was rejected by the committee. Mendes claims Vieira used a 'word game' to inappropriately suggest the CPI could indict for responsibility crimes, despite lacking factual basis, relevance to the CPI's scope, or legal grounding in criminal law.

item.title: Gastos de R$ 347 bi com precatórios ficarão de fora da meta até 2035
item.description: The Lula government proposed that R$ 347 billion in precatório payments be excluded from the primary surplus target until 2035, easing fiscal compliance. The plan includes a 0.5% of GDP primary surplus in 2027 (R$ 73.2 billion), with 10% of the precatório stock gradually incorporated into fiscal targets starting that year. The measure avoids cuts to discretionary spending and is supported by an extraordinary credit authorized by the STF through 2026.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz que Moraes vai desequilibrar eleições a partir do STF
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for President of Brazil, accused Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes of attempting to unbalance the 2026 elections through his judicial rulings. He claimed that Moraes’ actions are being used to favor one side in the political contest.

item.title: Trabalhadores apoiam proposta de Lula para reduzir jornada de trabalho
item.description: Thousands of workers marched in Brasília in support of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s proposal to reduce the workweek by four hours. The demonstration took place on October 15, aiming to pressure Congress to pass the bill. Lula, who is seeking re-election in 2026, is promoting the measure as part of his labor rights and quality-of-life agenda.

item.title: Governo revela previsões para PIB, taxa Selic e inflação em 2027. Confira
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's government will send to Congress the 2027 Budget Guidelines Bill (PLDO), projecting 2.56% GDP growth, 3.04% inflation, and a Selic rate of 10.55% by year-end. The document also forecasts a primary surplus of 0.5% of GDP (R$ 73.2 billion) and sets the foundation for the 2027 federal budget, including fiscal targets and minimum wage proposals.

item.title: Lula se reúne com representantes do Banco Santander
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva met with Santander’s global chair Ana Botín and Santander Brazil president Mário Leão at the Planalto Palace on April 15, 2026, without disclosing the meeting’s agenda. Over his third term, Lula has held official meetings with at least seven private bank executives, led by Bradesco’s Luiz Carlos Trabuco Cappi with five recorded visits, while other executives visited the presidency without appearing in the official schedule.

item.title: Alerj marca eleição de novo presidente para esta sexta-feira
item.description: The Legislative Assembly of the State of Rio de Janeiro (Alerj) has scheduled the election of a new president for this Friday, the 17th, following the annulment of former president Rodrigo Bacellar's mandate by the TSE. The vote aims to restore institutional stability in the state legislature amid ongoing uncertainty over the next governor, as the STF has postponed its ruling on whether the succession will be direct or indirect. In the meantime, the Guanabara Palace remains under the interim leadership of Ricardo Couto, president of the TJ-RJ, following Claudio Castro's resignation.

item.title: Boulos rebate relator de regulação de aplicativos: ‘Cedeu aos interesses das plataformas’
item.description: Minister Guilherme Boulos accused rapporteur Augusto Coutinho of yielding to platform interests in the app-based work regulation, making government support impossible. Minister José Guimarães announced the postponement of the vote due to lack of consensus in Congress. The dispute centers on the minimum wage for delivery workers, with the government advocating for R$ 10 and the rapporteur maintaining R$ 8,50.

item.title: O dedo de Lira para eleger um petista ao TCU
item.description: Deputy Arthur Lira (PP-AL) played a decisive role in the election of petista Odair Cunha (MG) to the Federal Court of Accounts (TCU), mobilizing votes and securing his approval with 303 votes. Odair’s candidacy was part of a political deal in which the PT supported Hugo Motta’s (Republicanos-PB) bid for Chamber presidency in 2025, in exchange for TCU backing. Despite Elmar Nascimento’s (BA) effort to siphon votes with PL support, Odair won comfortably, confirming the effectiveness of Lira and Motta’s political maneuvering.

item.title: Momento é difícil para o PT
item.description: Flavio Bolsonaro leads Lula for the first time in 2026 election polls, signaling a growing right-wing trend despite a technical tie. The PT faces a worrying scenario, as Lula never exceeds 45% in any poll and the left lacks a unified alternative, while the right consolidates around Flavio, whose voters are less affected by scandals like 'rachadinhas'. The race is expected to be extremely close in 2026, with Congress likely shifting further right, which could hinder a fourth Lula term or benefit a Flavio government.

item.title: Aliados de Flávio Bolsonaro comemoram Quaest, mas mantêm cautela sobre números
item.description: Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro celebrated the Quaest poll showing him ahead of Lula in a hypothetical second-round runoff (42% to 40%), interpreting it as a sign of sustained candidacy and federal government weariness. Despite the optimism, they remain cautious, noting Lula still leads in the first round (37% to 32%) and that attacks from opponents like Lindbergh Farias and André Janones have inadvertently boosted Bolsonaro’s numbers.

item.title: Messias intensifica “beija-mão” no Senado e visita 4 gabinetes em 1 dia
item.description: Union Attorney General Jorge Messias intensified his Senate lobbying to reverse opposition and win over undecided senators ahead of his Supreme Court nomination, visiting four offices in one day, including those of Leila Barros, Romário, Renan Filho, and Carlos Portinho. Despite these efforts, the opposition, led by PL and Novo, maintained a unified stance against his nomination, calling it a 'miracle' needing approval, with the hearing set for April 28.

item.title: Ministro das Comunicações quer fortalecer infraestrutura e ampliar inclusão digital no país
item.description: Communications Minister Frederico Siqueira declared 2026 as the 'year of delivery' for digital inclusion policies, aiming to expand connectivity infrastructure with R$23.6 billion in planned investments. He highlighted progress including 99,000 connected schools (72% of the 138,000 target), the Norte Conectado project installing 13,200 km of fiber optics in Amazonian riverbeds, and the goal of nationwide 4G coverage by 2028, all under legal certainty to attract investors. Deputy Maria Rosas questioned the feasibility of achieving these goals amid a tight budget and electoral calendar.

item.title: Governo propõe salário mínimo de R$ 1.717 em 2027
item.description: The Lula government proposed a minimum wage of R$ 1,717 for 2027, representing a nominal increase of 5.92%, as outlined in the 2027 Budget Guidelines Law Project (PLDO) submitted to Congress. The adjustment follows the formula of inflation (INPC projected at 3.06%) plus 2025 GDP growth, capped by the fiscal framework’s limit of real spending growth between 0.6% and 2.5% above inflation. Projections show the minimum wage rising to R$ 1,812 in 2028, R$ 1,913 in 2029, and R$ 2,020 in 2030, subject to future revisions.

item.title: Quem tem medo de André Mendonça?
item.description: Daniel Vorcaro’s plea bargain regarding the Banco Master scandal is under negotiation and may be finalized from May onward, sparking speculation in the STF about how André Mendonça, the case’s rapporteur, will pursue investigations against fellow justices. Although Mendonça enjoys strong ideological allies on the Court — such as Kassio Nunes Marques and Dias Toffoli — his ability to challenge Alexandre de Moraes is seen as limited unless more serious allegations emerge. His political survival within the tribunal will hinge on delivering impactful results without unduly damaging his allies, balancing public pressure with internal cohesion.

item.title: Governo limita crescimento de gasto com pessoal a 0,6% acima da inflação no Orçamento de 2027
item.description: The Lula government announced that the 2027 budget will include fiscal triggers to limit personnel spending growth to 0.6% above inflation and prohibit the expansion of tax benefits, following a primary deficit in 2023. The measure, mandated by a 2024 law, aims to contain the projected 4.2% nominal increase in payroll for 2027, attributed to public sector salary recomposition. The proposal also sets a primary surplus target of 0.5% of GDP, with a tolerance range of 0.25% to 0.75% of GDP.

item.title: Presidente da CPMI do INSS critica STF e fala em Corte política
item.description: Senator Carlos Viana (PSD-MG), president of the INSS CPMI, criticized the STF for assuming a political role in the country, claiming the Court treats authorities as friends or enemies without self-restraint or a respected ethical code. He argued that individual ministerial decisions block the work of nearly 600 elected parliamentarians and advocated for such rulings to be limited to collegial bodies. Viana also proposed structural reforms, including term limits for justices and greater inclusion of career judges in appointments, stating the issue should be discussed responsibly after the 2026 elections.

item.title: Senado aprova indicado do PT para TCU após votação na Câmara
item.description: The Senate approved the nomination of federal deputy Odair Cunha (PT-MG) for a vacancy in the Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU), a position reserved for the Chamber of Deputies. The vote took place on Wednesday, April 15, 2026, following deliberation in the lower house. The appointment strengthens the PT’s influence in Brazil’s external oversight institutions.

item.title: Nos EUA, Durigan tem reunião com Ilan Goldfajn, ex-Banco Central
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan met in Washington with former Central Bank president Ilan Goldfajn, now head of the Inter-American Development Bank, IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva, and Brazil's ambassador to the U.S., Maria Luisa Viotti. Durigan highlighted the IMF's upward revision of Brazil's growth forecast to 1.9%, underscoring the country's path of fiscal responsibility and sustainable growth. The meetings included strategic talks on investment, innovation, and international cooperation, with Durigan's international agenda extending through April 20, including engagements with President Lula in Spain and Germany.

item.title: Ministro do TSE nega ‘intervenção’ na Rede pedida por filiados
item.description: TSE Minister Floriano de Azevedo Marques rejected a petition for intervention in the Sustainability Network filed by dissident members, who accused the party leadership of antidemocratic and illegal practices. He ruled that the internal party dispute is unrelated to the electoral process and must be resolved by ordinary courts, also denying a request to sanction the members for bad-faith litigation.

item.title: Senado Federal aprova indicação do deputado petista Odair Cunha para o Tribunal de Contas da União
item.description: The Federal Senate approved the nomination of federal deputy Odair Cunha (PT-MG) to the Tribunal of Accounts of the Union (TCU) with 50 votes in favor, 8 against, and one abstention. The vacancy was part of a prior agreement to elect Hugo Motta as Chamber president, reserving the TCU seat for the PT following Aroldo Cedraz’s retirement.

item.title: Senado chancela candidato do governo ao TCU e carimba resultado já definido na Câmara
item.description: The Senate approved Odair Cunha's nomination to the TCU by a vote of 50 to 8, confirming the outcome already decided in the Chamber of Deputies, where the government had secured a comfortable majority despite opposition resistance. The Senate vote was seen as a procedural formality, given the strong support in the originating chamber and lack of effort to overturn the result. Cunha will assume the vacancy left by Aroldo Cedraz's retirement, concluding a process that was effectively settled after the Chamber's vote.

item.title: Oposição diz que STF ameaça o Congresso após fala de Gilmar sobre CPI
item.description: Opposition deputies accused Supreme Court ministers, particularly Gilmar Mendes and Dias Toffoli, of threatening Congress following their reactions to the Organized Crime CPI report, which called for the indictment of Court members. Gilmar’s remarks were interpreted as direct intimidation of Congress’s investigative authority, prompting symbolic protests by opposition lawmakers to defend the separation of powers.

item.title: Bolsonaristas querem enviar missão da Câmara aos EUA após a prisão de Ramagem
item.description: Bolsonarist deputies want to send a mission from the Chamber to the USA to supposedly monitor consular assistance to Brazilians after the arrest of Alexandre Ramagem. The trip would be funded with public resources.

item.title: Fim da escala 6 X 1 pode vigorar em julho e impulsionar Lula
item.description: Lula’s April 14 bill seeks to end the 6x1 work schedule and immediately implement a 5x2 schedule, potentially taking effect by July 15 if approved by Congress under constitutional urgency rules. The initiative aims to regain support from female voters, whose disapproval of the government surpassed approval in March, and will be highlighted in a national address on May 1 Labor Day. The administration views the constitutional urgency mechanism as a way to speed up legislative action, while acknowledging Congress’s autonomy in setting the vote pace.
